title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: GF VIII, the fourth draft of 'Analysis situs' (June–July 1986). This is Grothendieck's unpublished programme for an axiomatic, combinatorial 'tame topology' built from 'magasins' (stores) of cells with relations: incidence ◁/≤, an 'immersion/subdivision' relation ≪, and a disjointness relation |∘|. Page 1 lists the variants: general, local, faithful, punctual, maquettes, set-theoretic and tame magasins. This page adds orientation, defining 'magons orientés' (oriented multistructures).

Data of an oriented magon:
- a set M of cells;
- a relation ◁ (immediate incidence);
- a relation ≪̊;
- a disjointness relation |∘| ('open cells do not meet');
- a fixed-point-free involution X ↦ X⁻ ('the multistructure with opposite orientation');
- a subset M₀⁺ (the positively oriented points).
So M is the set of oriented cells: each geometric cell appears twice, as X and X⁻.

Axioms:
- Magon 1 (basic data).
  - (a) ◁ is antireflexive. The relation < it generates (X < Y iff there is a chain X ◁ X₁ ◁ … ◁ Xₙ = Y) is a strict order, so there are no closed chains. It satisfies the descending chain condition, so every X has finite dimension (length of maximal descending chains).
  - (b) ≪̊ is an order.
  - (c) |∘| is antireflexive.
  - (d) X ↦ X⁻ is an involution without fixed points.
  - (e) M₀⁺ ⊂ M.
- Magon 1′ (compatibility with orientation reversal).
  - X ◁ Y ⇒ X⁻ ◁ Y⁻.
  - X ≪ Y ⇒ X⁻ ≪ Y⁻.
  - X |∘| Y ⇒ X⁻ |∘| Y.
  - A marginal NB with a picture of a loop Y based at a point x warns that one can have both x ◁ Y and x⁻ ◁ Y. For a loop, ∂Y = x − x.
- Magon 2 (local compatibility of ≪ with incidence).
  - (a) An intermediate Y′ with X ≪ Y′ ≤ Y is unique.
  - (b) If X ≪ Y and X′ ◁ X, then there is Y′ ◁ Y with X′ ≪ Y′.
- Magon 3: disjointness passes to ≪-smaller cells.
- Magon 4: if X < Y then X |∘| Y. The open cell of a face is disjoint from the open cell it bounds.
- Magon 5 (positive points).
  - (a) Points of M₀⁺ have dimension 0.
  - (b) M₀ = M₀⁺ ⊔ (M₀⁺)⁻: every 0-cell has exactly one positive orientation.
- Magon 6 (oriented 'diamond' / ∂∂ = 0 condition).
  - (a) For Z < X of codimension 2 there is exactly one Y with Z ◁ Y ◁ X, and exactly one Y′ with Z⁻ ◁ Y′ ◁ X. So the two paths through the diamond carry opposite signs, which is the combinatorial form of ∂² = 0.
  - (b) A 1-cell X has exactly one positive vertex x ∈ M₀⁺ with x ◁ X. The other end enters as y⁻, so ∂X = x − y.
  - An arrow in the manuscript moves Magon 6 after Magon 5.

Purpose: to encode orientations and signed incidence numbers purely order-theoretically. Signs become an involution on cells rather than numbers, so that a chain complex / homology, and Stokes-type statements, can later be read off a magasin.
errors: Encoding incidence as a relation (not a multiplicity) cannot represent cell structures where a face occurs with multiplicity >1 (e.g. RP² = e⁰∪e¹∪e² with boundary word a·a; the relation only records Y◁X once, so ∂X=2Y is lost). The axioms thus effectively restrict to 'regular-like' oriented complexes; only the loop case (x and x⁻ both ◁ Y) is accommodated, as the marginal NB notes.

Magon 6a as written ('exactly one Y' for each sign') would forbid cellulations like S² = e⁰∪e² (codimension-2 incidence with no intermediate cell), unless the incidence relation is constrained elsewhere; the condition is a thinness/diamond hypothesis, not automatic.

Magon 1′c (X|∘|Y ⇒ X⁻|∘|Y) only states invariance in one variable; symmetry of |∘| is not stated here (the word 'symétrique' is crossed out in 1c), so one must either assume symmetry or add the second variable.
Numbering is inconsistent (Magon 6 placed before Magon 5, with an arrow indicating reordering); it is a working draft.

ideas.what: Oriented cells as elements of a set with a fixed-point-free involution (orientation reversal), with incidence between oriented cells replacing signed incidence numbers
ideas.modern_name: signed/oriented incidence posets; abstract cell complexes with incidence numbers (Tucker/Lefschetz style); oriented thin posets
ideas.usually_credited_to: A.W. Tucker (1933), S. Lefschetz (1942) for incidence-number axioms; later Björner, Basak (combinatorial cell complexes)

ideas.what: Oriented diamond axiom: for codimension-2 pairs there is exactly one intermediate cell with each sign, i.e. combinatorial ∂∂=0
ideas.modern_name: diamond property / thinness with sign condition (oriented thin posets, CW posets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Tucker, Lefschetz); diamond property in abstract polytopes (McMullen–Schulte), thin posets (Björner 1984)

ideas.what: Integration of orientation into the 'magasin' axiomatics (incidence, subdivision ≪, disjointness |∘|) of a combinatorial tame topology, with compatibility of ≪ with orientation and incidence (Magon 2–3)
ideas.modern_name: axiomatic combinatorial tame topology / subdivision structures on cell posets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Programme announced in Esquisse d'un programme (topologie modérée); no standard modern axiomatization
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) announces tame topology in general terms; the 'magasin' axioms themselves appear unpublished

ideas.what: Choice of a distinguished positive orientation of points (M₀⁺) and the convention that a 1-cell has exactly one positive endpoint

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an orientation layer ('magons orientés') on top of his unpublished 'magasin' axiomatics of tame topology. Orientation is encoded by a fixed-point-free involution, and a signed diamond axiom guarantees ∂²=0. It is also made compatible with the subdivision relation ≪ (Magon 1′b, Magon 2). The page sets this up but does not develop it into a homology/Stokes theory. A specialist might note the explicit coupling of orientation with subdivision maps inside an order-theoretic framework, which is not a standard object in the literature.
missed.quote: X ↦ X⁻ , involution ss pt fixe — "multistr. orientation opposée" … Magon 6 a) Soient Z < X, codim(X,Z)=2. Alors il n'existe qu'un seul Y′ avec Z ◁ Y′ ◁ X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of mostly historical interest. It documents how Grothendieck intended to make tame topology combinatorial, and could be compared with modern regular/directed complexes (Steiner, Hadzihasanovic) and oriented thin posets.

missed.claim: Oriented cells form an involutive set with incidence, a positive vertex per edge, and sign-alternating diamonds. Formally this sits very close to later 'directed complexes' and parity/pasting structures (Johnson 1989, Street 1991, Steiner 1993). Those also orient each face as input/output by a sign. Grothendieck, two years after Pursuing Stacks, does not draw this link here.
missed.quote: b) Soit X avec dim X = 1. Alors il existe un seul x ∈ M₀⁺, x ◁ X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a weak historical connection, not a result. It shows the same combinatorial device appearing independently in his tame-topology programme.

deep.surprise_reason: The page consists of draft definitions: an oriented version of his unpublished 'magasin' axioms using an orientation-reversing involution and a signed diamond condition. These are classical combinatorial devices (Tucker/Lefschetz incidence numbers, thin posets). They are interesting as documentation of the unpublished tame-topology programme, but contain no new theorem.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 annotations: under ◁̊ (dotted triangle) is written 'incidence immédiate'; under X ↦ X⁻ is 'involution ss pt fixe' and '"multistr. orientation opposée"'; M₀⁺ follows with a crossed-out word.
Magon 1a: 'Le préordre strict engendré <' (not 'La préordre … ≤'); the chain begins X₀ = X ◁̊ X₁.
Left margin (rotated): roughly 'Def. ◁ antiréflexive, relation stricte, condition des chaînes descendantes'; partly illegible.
Right marginal NB near Magon 1′: roughly 'NB On peut avoir à la fois x ◁ Y et x⁻ ◁ Y', illustrated by a loop Y at a point x. The transcription's 'X◁Y′' is a misreading.
Magon 2a: the word above 'alors Y′' is an insertion meaning 'unique'.
Magon 6a second clause: 'et un seul Y′ avec Z⁻ ◁ Y′ ◁ X' (sign on Z, not on X), consistent with ∂∂=0.
Magon 6b parenthetical is partly illegible; it does not read 'x = M₀'.
Magon 5b: 'M₀ = M₀⁺ ⊔ a(M₀⁺)', where a denotes the involution.
